output.summary: KEP-117 extends HPA metric specificity: adds a label selector to the Object and Pods metric sources, adds targetAverageValue to Object metrics, and aligns External sources with the new MetricIdentifier/MetricTarget form, delivered as a second autoscaling/v2 beta (v2beta2). The KEP's recorded status is implemented, stage stable, from 2020-12-28.
output.rationale: Users needed to select a specific series (e.g., one queue among several) from custom metrics without external relabeling, and to divide object targets by replica count. The design adds a selector to MetricIdentifier and a unified Target field, which requires a new beta API version. The discussion records a status-classification dispute: the KEP was declared implementable at alpha before PRR was required, and was retroactively marked implemented at beta, which skipped PRR review.

alternatives.option: Keep requiring out-of-band changes (e.g., Prometheus recording rules) to support complex metric environments
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this induces friction with Prometheus-style setups and often needs admin intervention that is not simple or scalable.

alternatives.option: Allow passing full queries instead of metric names
alternatives.why_not: The readme says it would add adapter complexity, security issues, and lesser portability, since adapters would need query rewriting to inject labels.

evidence.quote: This proposal brings both of those fields to the `Object` metric source type, and further brings the selector field to the `Pods` metric source type
These changes necessitate a second beta of `autoscaling/v2`: `autoscaling/v2beta2`.
This KEP was initially declared implementable at alpha, before PRR was required. The retroactive PR incorrectly called this "implemented" at beta
It landed after https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/2672 (which made PRR required for implementable), but since it landed as implemented, it skipped PRR
